data: Light, being the medium of most observations and measurements, is our window to the physical universe. In this course, we study geometrical optics, where light is described by rays. This deals with basic components like lenses, mirrors and prisms, from which instruments like telescopes and microscopes are built. In addition, we study the wave properties of light at an introductory level. It includes phenomena such as light interference that accounts for the colours on soap bubbles and has applications ranging from quantum studies to gravitational wave detection. We will also study polarization, which is of importance in photography. In addition, we will discuss diffraction, which is used extensively to study the crystal structure of solids.
